guard, force push.text:
yokoten stopped this: git push -f can overwrite the remote [force-push]

  Why       A plain force push can throw away work that someone else pushed.

  Instead   Use --force-with-lease, which stops when the remote has work you
            have not seen.

  More      https://github.com/yokoten-labs/yokoten/blob/main/docs/guide.md#the-core-rules

guard, wipe home.text:
yokoten stopped this: `rm` would wipe your home folder [wipe-home-or-system]

  Why       One command from an agent that lost its context can wipe the home
            folder or the system, and nothing brings the files back.

  Instead   Delete or change only files inside this project, and name each one.
            The guard refuses a wipe of home, of the system, or of a target it
            cannot read.

  More      https://github.com/yokoten-labs/yokoten/blob/main/docs/guide.md#the-safeguard

guard, tag push.text:
yokoten stopped this: git push origin v1.2.0 pushes a release tag [release]

  Why       Only the owner decides when to release.

  Instead   Stop and tell the owner: only the owner releases, with the steps in
            How to release; do not look for another way.

  More      https://github.com/yokoten-labs/yokoten/blob/main/docs/guide.md#how-to-release

yokoten: stage 1 of 5, safety net

  Next      No AGENTS.md, so the agents have no written rules here.

  Why       An agent follows the rules it can read, and only those.

  Fix       `yokoten init`

Tell the user in plain words, one step at a time, and offer to do it (as-is,
lighter, or not now with a reason).

yokoten: ~/.config/yokoten/private-marks is missing or has no marks

  Why       Without your marks, the privacy check knows only email addresses, IP
            addresses and secrets.

  Fix       `yokoten marks add`, then type your name, your city or a domain; it
            is not shown.

  More      https://github.com/yokoten-labs/yokoten/blob/main/docs/guide.md#privacy
